--- title: "Movement models" subtitle: WILD(FISH) 8390
Inference for Models of Fish and Wildlife Population Dynamics
## author: "Richard Chandler" ## date: "2025-11-18" format: revealjs: theme: default embed-resources: false toc: false toc-depth: 2 toc-title: Outline code-fold: false echo: true description: | Random walks --- # Overview {visibility="hidden"} ## Movement models ::: {.hidden} $$ \def\RR{{\bf R}} \def\bold#1{{\bf #1}} \def\but{{\boldsymbol u_t}} \def\butp{{\boldsymbol u_{t+1}}} \def\beps{{\boldsymbol \varepsilon}} $$ ::: - Random walks * Simple random walk * Correlated random walk * Biased random walk * Environmental gradients (PDEs) - Point process models * Step-selection models ::: {.notes} Speaker notes go here. ::: # Random walks ## Simple random walk
$$ {\boldsymbol u_{t+1}} = \but + \beps $$ where $$ {\boldsymbol \varepsilon} = \text{Norm}(0, \sigma^2 {\bf I}) $$ ## Simple random walk simulation {.smaller} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.cell code-block-bg='true'} ```{.r .cell-code style="font-size: 0.85em;"} sigma <- 0.05 T <- 50 u <- matrix(NA, nrow=T, ncol=2) u[1,] <- c(0.5,0.5) for(t in 2:T) { epsilon <- rnorm(n=2, mean=c(0,0), sd=sigma) u[t,] <- u[t-1,] + epsilon ## Equivalent to two lines above ## u[t,] <- rnorm(n=2, mean=u[t-1,], sd=0.05) } ``` :::
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code style="font-size: 0.85em;" code-fold="true"} plot(u, asp=1, xlim=c(0,1), ylim=c(0,1), xlab="", ylab="") arrows(u[1:49,1], u[1:49,2], u[2:50,1], u[2:50,2], length=0.1, col="blue") ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="54%"} ![](lecture-movement_files/figure-revealjs/fig-rw-simple-1.png){fig-align="top" width="100%"} ::: :::: ## Biased random walk ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'}
$$ {\boldsymbol u_{t+1}} = \but + {\bf B}(\but-{\boldsymbol s}) + \beps $$ where, typically: $$ \begin{equation} {\bf B} = \begin{pmatrix} \rho & 0 \\ 0 & \rho \end{pmatrix} \end{equation} $$ with $\rho \in [0,1]$
::: {.fragment}
Treating $\boldsymbol s$ as an activity center opens possibilities for joint SCR movement models for true population-level inference on movement and density/demography.
::: ::: ## Biased random walk simulation :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="45%"} ::: {style='font-size: 65%;'}
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="1-11"} sigma <- 0.05 rho <- 0.1 # Bias towards activity center T <- 50 u <- matrix(NA, nrow=T, ncol=2) u[1,] <- c(0.5,0.5) s <- c(0.5,0.5) B <- diag(rho,2) for(t in 2:T) { epsilon <- rnorm(n=2, mean=c(0,0), sd=sigma) u[t,] <- u[t-1,] + B%*%(s-u[t-1,]) + epsilon } par(mai=c(0.7,0.7,0.1,0.1)) plot(u, asp=1, xlim=c(0,1), ylim=c(0,1), xlab="", ylab="") points(s[1], s[2], pch=16, col=rgb(0,0,1,0.9), cex=2.5) arrows(u[1:49,1], u[1:49,2], u[2:50,1], u[2:50,2], length=0.1, col="blue") ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="55%"} ![](lecture-movement_files/figure-revealjs/brw-simple-1.png){width="100%"} ::: ::: ## Correlated random walk
$$ \butp = \but + {\bf R}(\but-{\boldsymbol u}_{t-1}) + \beps $$ where $$ {\bf R} = \gamma \begin{pmatrix} \cos(\theta) & -\sin(\theta) \\ \sin(\theta) & \cos(\theta) \end{pmatrix} $$ with $\theta \in [-\pi,\pi]$ being the expected turn angle, and $\gamma \in [0,1]$ dampening the persistence. ## Correlated random walk simulation ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="45%"} ::: {style='font-size: 65%;'}
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="1-16"} sigma <- 0.05 gamma <- 0.8 ## Damping of correlated walk theta <- 0 ## Correlation (-pi,pi) T <- 50 u <- matrix(NA, nrow=T, ncol=2) u[1,] <- c(0.5,0.5) u[2,] <- rnorm(2, u[1,], sd=0.05) R <- gamma*matrix(c(cos(theta),sin(theta), -sin(theta),cos(theta)), nrow=2, ncol=2) for(t in 3:T) { epsilon <- rnorm(n=2, mean=c(0,0), sd=sigma) u[t,] <- u[t-1,] + R%*%(u[t-1,]-u[t-2,]) + epsilon } par(mai=c(0.7,0.7,0.1,0.1)) plot(u, asp=1, xlim=range(u[,1]), ylim=range(u[,2]), xlab="", ylab="") arrows(u[1:49,1], u[1:49,2], u[2:50,1], u[2:50,2], length=0.1, col="blue") ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="55%"} ![](lecture-movement_files/figure-revealjs/fig-crw-simple-1.png){width="100%"} ::: ::: ## Behavioral state switching ::: {style='font-size: 90%;'}
$$ \butp = \begin{cases} \but + \beps & \text{if} \qquad m_t=1 \\ \but + {\bf R}(\but-{\boldsymbol u}_{t-1}) + \beps & \text{if} \qquad m_t=2 \end{cases} $$ with: $$ m_t \sim \mathrm{Categorical}(\pi_1, \pi_2) $$
::: {.fragment}
Possible to have more than 2 states, but additional information (eg, accelerometer data) often needed.
::: ::: ## Behavioral state switching simulation ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="45%"} ::: {style='font-size: 65%;'} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="1-24"} sigma <- 0.05 gamma <- 0.8 ## Damping of correlated walk theta <- 0 ## Correlation (-pi,pi) psi <- 0.2 ## Pr(correlated walk) probs <- c(psi, 1-psi) T <- 50 u <- matrix(NA, nrow=T, ncol=2) u[1,] <- c(0.5,0.5) u[2,] <- rnorm(2, u[1,], sd=0.05) R <- gamma*matrix(c(cos(theta),sin(theta), -sin(theta),cos(theta)), nrow=2, ncol=2) m <- rep(1, T) for(t in 3:T) { m[t] <- which(rmultinom(1, 1, probs)==1) epsilon <- rnorm(n=2, mean=c(0,0), sd=sigma) if(m[t]==1) { u[t,] <- u[t-1,] + epsilon } else if(m[t]==2) { u[t,] <- u[t-1,] + R%*%(u[t-1,]-u[t-2,]) + epsilon } } par(mai=c(0.7,0.7,0.1,0.1)) plot(u, asp=1, xlim=range(u[,1]), ylim=range(u[,2]), col=c("black", "orange")[m], xlab="", ylab="") arrows(u[1:49,1], u[1:49,2], u[2:50,1], u[2:50,2], length=0.1, lwd=c(1,2)[m], col=c("black", "orange")[m]) legend(0.5, -1, c("Foraging", "Traveling"), lwd=1:2, col=c("black", "orange"), lty=1, pch=1, cex=1.5) ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="55%"} ![](lecture-movement_files/figure-revealjs/fig-crw-behave-1.png){width="100%"} ::: ::: ## [Random walks along environmental gradients]{style="font-size: 80%;"}
::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} $$ \butp = \but + {\bf D}\nabla x(\but) + \beps $$ where $\bf D = \alpha {\bf I}$ is a $2\times2$ matrix describing the effect of the gradient in the environment ($\nabla x$) at location $\but$.
::: {.fragment} Positive values of $\alpha$ describe the scenario in which the organism tends to move in the direction of the gradient. If $\alpha=0$, the individual will ignore the environment as it follows a simple random walk. :::
::: {.fragment} Natural method for studying resource selection and space use. ::: ::: ## Environment
::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(430) library(terra) delta <- 0.025 ## Resolution grid0 <- seq(delta/2, 1-delta/2, delta) grid <- cbind(rep(grid0, each=length(grid0)), rep(grid0, times=length(grid0))) distmat <- as.matrix(dist(grid)) ## Distance b/w grid points npixels <- nrow(distmat) V <- exp(-0.1*distmat) ## Covariance R <- chol(V) X <- t(R) %*% rnorm(npixels) ## Gaussian random field Xr <- rast(cbind(grid, X), type="xyz", ## Convert to raster crs="+proj=utm +zone=17 +datum=NAD83 +units=m +no_defs +type=crs") terr <- terrain(Xr, v=c("slope","aspect"), unit="radians") ## Slope and aspect vfieldU <- terr$slope * sin(terr$aspect) ## x-coord of arrow head vfieldV <- terr$slope * cos(terr$aspect) ## y-coord of arrow head vfieldData <- cbind(as.data.frame(Xr, xy=TRUE), v1=values(vfieldU), v2=values(vfieldV)) names(vfieldData) <- c("s1","s2","X","v1","v2") ``` ::: ::: ## [Simulating random walks along environmental gradients]{style="font-size: 60%;"}
::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(311409) T <- 50 uERW <- matrix(0.5, T, 2) ## Initial location alpha <- 0.02; D <- diag(alpha,2) ## Effect of envi gradient xmin <- ymin <- 0+delta; xmax <- ymax <- 1-delta ## Bounds enviro <- numeric(T) ## Environment along path enviro[1] <- as.numeric(extract(Xr, uERW[1,,drop=FALSE])) for(t in 2:T) { ulast <- uERW[t-1,,drop=FALSE] grad <- as.numeric(c(extract(vfieldU, ulast), extract(vfieldV, ulast))) unew <- ulast + t(D%*%grad) + rnorm(2, 0, sigma) if(unew[1]xmax) unew[1] <- xmax-(unew[1]-xmax) if(unew[2]ymax) unew[2] <- ymax-(unew[2]-ymax) uERW[t,] <- unew ## New location enviro[t] <- as.numeric(extract(Xr, unew)) ## Environment at new location } ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ::: ## [Simulating random walks along environmental gradients]{style="font-size: 60%;"} ![](lecture-movement_files/figure-revealjs/pde-fig-1.png){width="100%"} # Point process models ## Step selection models ## Summary Technical treatment of movement models for telemetry data given in [Hooten et al. 2017](https://www.routledge.com/Animal-Movement-Statistical-Models-for-Telemetry-Data/Hooten-Johnson-McClintock-Morales/p/book/9781032097183).
See [Mcclintock et al. 2002](https://doi.org/10.1002/ecy.3473) and related papers in the special issue of Ecology on joint movement and SCR models.
Consider random walks as alternatives to GLMM approximations of step-selection models.

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
